attributes.provenance: Landed 2026-09-01 in worktree GDL-Claude-WfMulti, branch claude/wf-multiwindow-20260901, commit b18562d7b. tools/gdl/webfrank.py: new verify_relocation_binding(), wired into permute_instruction_atoms and supplied unconditionally by apply_patch for every window. equivalent_copy_form's relocation screen normalised to word indexes. 15 new tests (RelocationBindingTests + three EquivalentCopyFormTests); all three copy-form tests were confirmed FAILING against the old code before the fix, so the gap was demonstrated reachable rather than assumed. subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value: THE TWO REPORTED WEBFRANK GUARD GAPS ARE CLOSED IN CODE, AND CLOSING THE SECOND ONE CORRECTED A PREMISE IN THE LAW THAT REPORTED IT. GAP 1, closed as specified: claim.law.HV_emb-sda21-relocation-offset-differs-between-our-objects-and-the-target.20260901.v1 was exactly right that equivalent_copy_form screened relocations by EXACT byte offset while MWCC records EMB_SDA21 at word+2, so a relocated word passed the 'not a copy-form candidate' precondition. Both sides are now normalised with `offset // 4` and the screen tests the whole word RANGE. The live instance the law names, pbWinSetup +0x314 (`addi r3,r3,lbl_801284D8@l`, ADDR16_LO at 790 with the word at 788), is now a regression test and is refused. GAP 2, closed with a CORRECTION worth carrying: claim.law.HV_permute-payload-check-does-not-bind-a-relocation-to-its-atom.20260901.v1 is correct that the sorted `(offset % 4, info, addend)` multiset proves CONSERVATION and never BINDING, and its prescribed fix - carry each atom's (type, symbol) through the permutation and assert it against the target's relocation at the destination - is what shipped. BUT ITS IMPLIED KEY-SET EQUALITY IS FALSE, AND THE FIRST BUILD PROVED IT: dtk RESOLVES ADDRESSES WHEN IT EXTRACTS THE RETAIL OBJECT, so a word we still carry as ADDR16_HA/ADDR16_LO can appear in the target as an already-baked literal with NO relocation at all. game/g3d/gcontrolpads::G3DReadControlPadStates is the live instance (its own shipped rule prose documents the gPadManager halves), and a binding check demanding equal relocation sets on both sides fails it. THE CORRECT ASYMMETRY: a word relocated in the TARGET but not in ours is never benign and always fails; a word relocated in OURS but not the target is exempt from the cross-object test, but ONLY when nothing in the window could have been exchanged with it. That side condition is what keeps the exemption from reopening the hole, and it is cheap and exact: an exchange can only survive into byte-correct text when the two atoms are identical OUTSIDE their register fields, since the recolor stage that runs afterwards can rewrite nothing else. So the unbindable atom must be unique in the window under `word & ~register_slot_mask(word)`, with the widest register mask assumed for any unmodelled form so the fallback fails closed. SECOND CORRECTION, also found by the build: an EXACT symbol-name match must bind directly whatever the name looks like. Our objects frequently carry the target's own `lbl_XXXXXXXX` placeholder spelling for an own-pool datum (live instance game/game/combat +0x4, lbl_80240E30 on both sides), so a naive 'target-pool-label names must go through the pool correspondence' rule rejects identical names. Differing names are accepted only as a pool correspondence: ours spelled `@NNNN`, the target's `lbl_`/`jumptable_`, required CONSISTENT AND ONE-TO-ONE across the whole window, which is what forbids an exchange among them. Equal names are also recorded in that correspondence so a later differing pair in the same window cannot contradict them. THE GUARD FIRES ON REAL DATA, which is the evidence it is not decorative: both corrections above were discovered by shipped rules failing the first version of the check, not by inspection. The obligation the HV law placed on whoever DERIVES an order is now discharged by the tool for every permutation apply_patch runs, and the pb_window rules exercise the pool-correspondence path for real (@37 <-> lbl_80349018, @109 <-> lbl_80349050).
